{"id": "60b98d4b-b3f1-412f-b184-eb0c9b50b15f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Based on the AWS documentation:

**PipelinesLocked = 0** means at least one pair of eligible pipelines on the channel is **not synchronized** (i.e., not frame-accurate with each other). A value of 1 would mean all eligible pipeline pairs are synchronized. This applies to a STANDARD channel configured for standard pipeline locking (the default mode).

**Output group types pipeline locking applies to:**

With the default **source timecode** method, pipeline locking applies to:
- HLS (Live mode)
- MediaPackage
- CMAF Ingest
- UDP and SRT (segmented outputs only)
- Microsoft Smooth

With **video aligned locking** (the visual-signature-based method, used when timecodes are unreliable or unavailable), it applies to the same set minus Microsoft Smooth:
- HLS (Live mode)
- MediaPackage
- CMAF Ingest
- UDP and SRT (segmented only)

If a channel's output types aren't among the applicable ones, the `PipelinesLocked` metric simply doesn't apply and will always read 0 regardless of actual sync state — so a 0 is only meaningful when at least one eligible output type is in use.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

**PipelinesLocked = 0** means at least one pair of eligible pipelines on the channel is **not synchronized** (i.e., not frame-accurate with each other). A value of 1 would mean all eligible pipeline pairs are synchronized. This applies to a STANDARD channel configured for standard pipeline locking (the default mode).

**Output group types pipeline locking applies to:**

With the default **source timecode** method, pipeline locking applies to:
- HLS (Live mode)
- MediaPackage
- CMAF Ingest
- UDP and SRT (segmented outputs only)
- Microsoft Smooth

With **video aligned locking** (the visual-signature-based method, used when timecodes are unreliable or unavailable), it applies to the same set minus Microsoft Smooth:
- HLS (Live mode)
- MediaPackage
- CMAF Ingest
- UDP and SRT (segmented only)

If a channel's output types aren't among the applicable ones, the `PipelinesLocked` metric simply doesn't apply and will always read 0 regardless of actual sync state — so a 0 is only meaningful when at least one eligible output type is in use."}]}
